note: issue 657 (CON-1): one strategy per problem, kept once chosen. Derived from the code as of this issue; see docs/decisoes/0026-result-and-route-error-format.md. test/architecture-registers.test.mjs checks that the eight problems are present and each reference exists.

result.decision: An expected failure is returned as { ok: true, ...value } | { ok: false, reason: <english_code>, ...detail }; throw only for a broken invariant (decision 0026). No shared type yet: each function declares its own union.
result.ratchet: new code; legacy shapes (param, error, why) are migrated in a separate issue

error-format.decision: A route answers failure with send(res, status, { error, reason? }): error is the message the person reads (or a stable code), reason is a stable english code; never a stack, never an upstream or raw error (decision 0026).
error-format.ratchet: new code; the 500 handler in api/server.ts already answers { error } with no detail

http-client.decision: Outbound HTTP uses the global fetch (Node 24) with AbortSignal.timeout (redirect: error where the host is fixed) and takes the fetch as an injectable option so tests replace it. node:http request stays for the loopback core only.
http-client.ratchet: new code; transcription/install.ts calls fetch without a timeout (legacy)

validation.decision: Hand-written guards at the boundary (isText, isIssueKey, parse functions returning a union); no schema library is a dependency of the packages.
validation.ratchet: new code; a schema library would be a new decision record

test.decision: node:test with node:assert/strict, run by node --test; package tests are .test.ts beside the folder layout under packages/nucleo/test, repository guards are .mjs under test/.

date-time.decision: Instants are ISO-8601 UTC strings (toISOString) in storage and JSON, epoch milliseconds (Date.now) inside rate and timing logic; the clock is a parameter (now) where a test must control it.
date-time.ratchet: new code takes now as a parameter; direct new Date() calls in legacy code stay

persistence.decision: Local state lives in SQLite through node:sqlite (synchronous, STRICT tables) behind the storage port; every write runs in one immediateTransaction (BEGIN IMMEDIATE, commit or rollback); append-only by preference, otherwise upsert with history near the entity (table-modes.json).
persistence.ratchet: new tables are append-only or upsert-with-history; upsert tables are flagged legacy

events.decision: Session events are appended once by stable id (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) with a monotonic seq; clients follow changes through the cursor (long poll and SSE), resuming by cursor, never by offset.
